sentences.text:
The matter is listed for hearing on I.As and with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties,
the matter is taken up for consideration.

2. This appeal is filed challenging the order dated 23.06.2016 passed in LAC No.5/2007 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bantwal, Dakshina Kannada, allowing the reference petition for enhanced compensation.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bantwal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Reference Court has given the finding that the respondent has perfected his title by way of adverse possession.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that without making the State as party to the proceedings, an order has been passed and the respondent is also claiming adverse possession against the State.
In the absence of State being made as party to the proceedings, the Reference Court ought not to have given the finding.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent would submit that this is a third round of litigation before this Court and NC: 2023:KHC:24727 earlier, this Court also directed the Reference Court to decide the issue between the parties with regard to adverse possession in W.P.No.22669/2012 vide order dated 21.06.2012.
Hence, the order impugned is passed by the Reference Court.

5. Having heard the respective counsel and also on perusal of the material available on record, it is not in dispute that the property belonging to the respondent was acquired and the respondent claims that he is in possession of the same.

However, the issue between the parties was also referred to the Reference Court and no doubt, the Reference Court also given the finding that the respondent has perfected his title by way of adverse possession, on perusal of the order impugned before this Court, it is seen that the State has not been made as party to the proceedings and the respondent herein has made only the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Housing Board as party to the proceedings.

Admittedly, the property belongs to the State Government and when the respondent is claiming adverse possession, in the absence of the State being made as party to the proceedings,
finding given by the Reference Court NC: 2023:KHC:24727 in LAC No.5/2007 is not correct.

Hence,
it is appropriate to set aside the order and remand the matter to the reference Court.

6. Accordingly, I pass the following:
The Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Mrs. Seetharathana K. Bhat on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164724171/
2 ORDER

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer vs Mrs. Seetharathana K. Bhat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The appeal is allowed.
(ii) The order dated 23.06.2016 passed in LAC No.5/2007 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Bantwal, Dakshina Kannada, is hereby set aside.

(iii) The respondent herein is directed to make the State as party to the proceedings forthwith and after impleading the State, the Reference Court shall decide the issue involved between the parties with regard to adverse possession as claimed by the respondent herein.
(iv) The appellant and the respondent shall appear before the Reference Court on 18.08.2023, without expecting any notice.
(v) The Reference Court is directed to dispose of the matter within six months from 18.08.2023.

(vi) The Registry is directed to send the records to the Reference Court, forthwith, to enable NC:
2023:KHC:24727 the Reference Court to take up the matter on 18.08.2023.

Sd/-
